rawFindings.title: Windows absolute local paths are still treated as cacheable
rawFindings.explanation: The new local-source check only recognizes paths beginning with a slash, backslash, ./, ../, or file:// followed by a slash. A Windows absolute path such as `C:\work\dep` or `C:/work/dep` does not match, so `isNotCacheable()` returns false even though it is a local dependency. PackageRepository will then use and store this dependency in the resolve cache, allowing stale cached contents to be returned for a changed local package.
rawFindings.suggestion: Recognize drive-letter absolute paths as local as well, e.g. include `/^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/` or normalize/strip file prefixes and use an absolute-path helper appropriate for Windows.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: On Windows, fetch a dependency with source `C:\work\dep`, then modify files in that local package and fetch it again with the same target; the second fetch may come from the resolve cache instead of the current local directory contents.
